task.description: CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR hard gate (WF-02 Step 1b) on REQ-171's design (lib/letflow/design/req171-wasm-host-api-read.md, test/specs/REQ-171.md). This is the FIRST requirement wiring together all four previously-shipped WASM modules (ModuleRegistry, CapabilityGate, MemoryGuard, ResourceLimits) into a real host function dispatch -- the most structurally complex WASM design this pipeline has produced. It reports several live-verified findings about wasmex's real callback ABI (argument shape, return shape, error behavior) and one genuine cross-runtime divergence (Lua denies a capability at call-time; WASM's design denies at instantiation-time) flagged as a finding for you/REVIEWER/SECURITY-REVIEWER, not silently resolved. Independently verify the central claims -- do not rubber-stamp given the integration complexity, but also don't re-verify what REQ-165-170's own gates already settled (module_registry.ex/capability_gate.ex/memory_guard.ex/resource_limits.ex's own contracts are already gate-approved; focus your live verification on the NEW claims this design makes about wiring them together).
acceptance_criteria: Independently reproduce the design's live-verified claim about a host callback's real argument shape ([context | params] with plain Elixir integers for :i32 args) and the context map's real shape (%{memory:, caller:, pid:, instance:}) against the real installed wasmex.

Independently reproduce the claim that a single-result callback must return a BARE value (not a list), and confirm what happens when a callback raises or returns a type-mismatched value (the design claims both collapse into an opaque {:error, binary()} without crashing the GenServer -- verify this carefully, since a crash here would be a much more severe finding).

Confirm context.caller/context.memory genuinely provide what MemoryGuard.read/4 and write/4 require as their Wasmex.StoreOrCaller.t()/Wasmex.Memory.t() arguments -- read memory_guard.ex's real @spec and confirm the types actually line up.
Confirm the uuid decision (documented WASM-side addition, :none-gated like now) is reasonable and the moduledoc states it plainly, not silently.
Confirm the number-marshalling decision (reuse LuaNumberMarshalling.to_lua/1 directly, no second rule) is sound given the design's own reasoning about read_variable crossing as JSON bytes.

Confirm the capability-gating extension (a new build_import_table/2 with a :none sentinel, layered over REQ-167's existing build_import_table/1) is a genuine, careful extension and not a silent second capability model -- read capability_gate.ex's real current contract and confirm the extension is additive, not a redefinition.

CAREFULLY evaluate the flagged cross-runtime divergence (Lua denies at call-time, WASM denies at instantiation-time per this design) -- is this a real, unavoidable consequence of the two runtimes' structural differences (Lua's dynamic dispatch vs. WASM's static import-table-at-instantiation model), or is it a design choice that could be reconciled to match Lua's call-time semantics? Reason through this carefully -- this is exactly the kind of 'genuine semantic conflict' REQ-171's own text says must be raised as a finding, not resolved by moving the Lua side, but you should confirm the finding itself is accurate and not overstated or understated.

Confirm the guest-owns-the-buffer string-return protocol (design's stated >=0/-1/-2 sentinel scheme) avoids the re-entrant host-calls-guest-alloc hazard it claims to avoid -- reason through the actual call sequence.
Confirm the tenant-prefix/execution_context closure-capture mechanism is genuinely never guest-derived, per decision 0014(e).
Full traceability table covers every real REQ-171 acceptance criterion from docs/requirements.yaml.
Zero literal Elixir implementation code in the design doc.
CRITICAL: the handoff's top-level status field (line 9) must be exactly PENDING/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED/FAILED/ESCALATED/CANCELLED when you finish -- run mix letflow.lint_handoffs before finishing.

result.summary: REQ-171 design (lib/letflow/design/req171-wasm-host-api-read.md) and test/specs/REQ-171.md PASS the design gate. All 12 acceptance criteria independently checked; no blocking defect found.
verification_performed: Reproduced Finding 1 (context shape %{memory:, caller:, pid:, instance:}; callback invoked as apply(callback, [context | params]) with plain Elixir integers for :i32 args) live via a fresh scratch script against the real installed wasmex v0.15.1 (WASMEX_BUILD=true, ASDF/cargo PATH), and independently by reading deps/wasmex/lib/wasmex.ex's handle_info({:invoke_callback, ...}) clause (lines ~541-576) directly -- matches the design's own citation verbatim.

Reproduced Finding 2 (single-result callback must return a BARE value; wasmex wraps it into a one-element list; a manually double-wrapped [99] return produces a trap, not a crash) live -- {:ok, [99]}-equivalent for a bare-int callback, and a clean {:error, ...} trap (never a crash) for a callback that itself returns [99] for a single-result import.

Reproduced Finding 3 (a raising callback and a type-mismatched return both collapse into an opaque {:error, "Error during function excecution: ..."} string, and the owning Wasmex GenServer stays alive) live -- Process.alive?/1 confirmed true after both failure modes. Cross-checked the literal 'Error during function excecution' string against deps/wasmex/native/wasmex/src/{instance,caller,component_instance}.rs, confirming it is the genuine Rust-side message, not a paraphrase.

Confirmed context.caller/context.memory line up with MemoryGuard.read/4's real @spec (Wasmex.StoreOrCaller.t(), Wasmex.Memory.t(), integer(), integer()) by reading lib/letflow/engine/wasm/memory_guard.ex directly, then live-drove MemoryGuard.read/4 with context.caller/context.memory inside a real callback -- returned the correct bytes on success and the correct {:invalid_pointer, {:length_exceeds_memory, ...}} on an out-of-bounds read, which the design's own -2 sentinel path consumes correctly.

Read lib/letflow/engine/wasm/capability_gate.ex's real current contract: @known_imports has exactly 2 placeholder rows, import_descriptor() currently has capability :: capability() (no :none), stub_callback/0 is literally fn _context, _arg1, _arg2 -> 0 end (bare 0, matching the design's Finding 2 citation), and build_import_table/1's filter is Enum.filter(&MapSet.member?(granted, &1.capability)). The design's widened capability_requirement() type and always-include-:none fold are additive to this, not a redefinition -- confirmed genuine.

Read lib/letflow/engine/lua/platform.ex directly: @capability_matrix's now/fail rows use required: :none (lines 350-351) and required_capability(:none, _args), do: :none (line 490) exist verbatim as cited; install/1, install/2, install/3 all exist as claimed, supporting the design's build_import_table/1 -> /2 mirroring claim.

Read lib/letflow/engine_lua_number_marshalling.ex: to_lua/1 and from_lua/1 are both literal identity functions (def to_lua(value), do: value) -- confirms the design's premise that to_lua/1 is encoding-agnostic and safe to reuse ahead of Jason.encode!/1 for read_variable's JSON-bytes transport, with no second numeric rule introduced.

Confirmed decision-record quotes: docs/migration/decisions/0014-*.md line ~178 ('the Lua host API is the definition WASM conforms to') and line ~348 ('Host functions receive already-resolved values; the tenant prefix...') both match the design's citations verbatim.

Carefully evaluated the flagged cross-runtime divergence (Lua denies at call-time; WASM denies at instantiation-time). Re-read WASM-06's own acceptance text in docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-167 entry: 'Imports outside the whitelist MUST cause INSTANTIATION TO FAIL' -- this is REQ-167/WASM-06's own already-gate-approved MUST-level acceptance criterion, not merely an implementation choice REQ-171 could reconcile within its own scope. The design's framing ('inherent to REQ-167's already-approved architecture, not introduced or fixable by this requirement') is accurate -- it correctly avoids overclaiming this is an unavoidable law of WASM itself (a call-time-gating WASM design is technically possible) while correctly identifying that changing it would mean reopening REQ-167/WASM-06's own locked acceptance criteria, which is out of REQ-171's scope. The finding is neither overstated nor understated, and is correctly routed to REVIEWER/SECURITY-REVIEWER via OQ-4 rather than silently resolved.

Traced the guest-owns-the-buffer protocol's call sequence: guest supplies (out_ptr, out_cap) up front; the host never calls a guest alloc export; a too-small out_cap returns n with zero bytes written, requiring the guest to call again with its own buffer -- no host-initiated re-entrant call into guest code occurs at any point, consistent with wasmex's own store-vs-caller deadlock warning the design cites.

Confirmed execution_context is documented as supplied only via build_import_table/2's closure capture at call time (never guest-derived, never read from guest memory), consistent with decision 0014(e)'s quoted text, and that INV-HOSTAPI-4 states this as a binding invariant.

Cross-checked the design's own traceability table (design section 9) and test/specs/REQ-171.md's traceability table against docs/requirements.yaml's real REQ-171 entry (9 acceptance criteria, verbatim) -- all 9 are covered by name and text, none paraphrased away or dropped.
Grepped the design doc for 'def '/function bodies -- none found; every code block is @spec/@type/table-shaped, satisfying 'design artefact only, no implementation code.'
result.gaps_found: None blocking. Two non-blocking observations, both already explicitly surfaced by the design itself and not requiring rework: (1) OQ-4's instantiation-vs-call-time divergence is correctly flagged rather than fixed, and this validator confirms REVIEWER/SECURITY-REVIEWER is the correct next owner, not CODE-DESIGNER. (2) The uuid WASM-only decision (AC5) is stated plainly in design section 3 with three explicit reasons and a candidate-finding note for ORCH, not silently implemented as parity -- reasonable as written.
result.verdict: PASS -- design and test spec approved to proceed to WF-02's next step (ELIXIR-DEV implementation).
